Independent certificate uses an explicitly isomorphic alternative graph labeling, a degree-one-peeling forest test, and pairwise intersection adjacency, and matches every one of the 3,173,940 unordered distances. A graph-theoretic edge-count argument proves the minimum size is at least six. Generated group of order 120, explicit representatives and orbit closure verify all 180 exceptional pairs, their unique partner and per-edge incidence. Both actual package programs executed successfully.

originality.rationale: The novel portion is the exchange-excess count by overlap, the 180 exceptional pairs forming a matching, the 6-per-edge localization, and the three full-symmetry orbits. Prior general results address optimum feedback-set cardinality or connectedness/bounded reachability, and previously accessible exact data on this graph establish total states, exchange edges, and diameter but not the exceptional-pair classification. value.rationale: The natural Johnson lower bound measures necessary exchanges before feasibility constraints. The 180 genuine maximum-excess obstructions are not arbitrary table entries: they form a uniquely partnered matching on only 360 configurations and are uniformly localized to every original dodecahedral edge, in exactly three symmetry orbits. This determines the rare precise circumstances where shortest feasibility-preserving exchange requires two additional moves, finer than connectedness, diameter, or simple state count.
